I would make no file changes and dispatch no fix subagent this round. The only fix the review identifies is a one-line change in `vendor/gtfs_lite/calendar.py`, and the plan's Global Constraints say "Do not edit anything under `vendor/`; a script syncs it from upstream." That is an explicit scope fence. A ruling never crosses a fence, so I stop and ask. No fix attempt is spent, and Task 4 stays unmarked in the ledger.

Before asking, I would run one read-only check to confirm the reviewer's diagnosis:

<command>
sed -n '80,95p' vendor/gtfs_lite/calendar.py
</command>

<command>
grep -rn "exception_type" vendor/gtfs_lite/ ferry/
</command>

The message I would send my partner:

> Task 4 (`runs_on`, commit 7c1d9e0) matches its brief, but the review found a real bug that I can't fix inside the plan's rules.
>
> `vendor/gtfs_lite/calendar.py:88` compares `exception_type` to the string `'1'`, while the parser yields the integer `1`. As a result every removal exception is read as an addition, and `runs_on` returns True on 2026-12-25. The parsed objects are frozen, so nothing outside `vendor/` can correct the value. The plan's Global Constraints forbid editing `vendor/`, because a script syncs it from upstream, so I've stopped without making any change.
>
> How do you want to proceed?
> 1. **Recommended:** fix it upstream and re-run the sync script. Nothing in this branch has to bend the constraint.
> 2. Allow a local one-line patch to line 88 (`'1'` → `1`) for this branch. The next sync will overwrite it unless upstream has the fix by then.
> 3. Amend the plan so `runs_on` reads the raw calendar-dates data directly instead of the parsed calendar. That is a design change, so I'd want your sign-off first.
>
> Once you choose, I'll dispatch the fix as round 1 with the covering test `tests/test_exceptions.py` and then run the scoped re-review. Tasks after 4 wait on this.
